summary.source: Live code read against the rendered S105 startup brief, the git history of context/LATEST_HANDOFF.md across twelve closeouts, and an executed ten-season runRealismVerification on the canonical seed 20260306.
summary.verificationNote: Every premise below was checked against live code before inclusion. Item 1's premise was checked against every committed handoff since S96: none has ever matched the parser.

profile.rubric: product; game-loop payoff, truthful feedback, static-host safety and measured release readiness
profile.staging: Stable Cloudflare staging before authorized main promotion and production deployment
profile.source: arc-profile (studio-ops copy, --project .; no local copy exists), context/PROJECT_STATUS.json, context/LATEST_HANDOFF.md

items.title: One of the three session authorities has never been read: the handoff heading this project writes matches neither parser
items.premise: resolveSessionAuthority takes the monotonic maximum of SIL, status and handoff and flags divergence when they disagree. parseHandoffCloseoutAuthority only recognises '# Session N Closeout', and brief-semantic-fingerprint only recognises 'Where We Left Off (Session N)'. This project has headed every handoff '# Latest Handoff — Session N → Session N+1' since at least S96, so the brief has rendered 'handoff=S?' for the project's whole recorded history and the divergence check has silently been a two-way check. A handoff lagging SIL by a session could never be detected.

premises.claim: The closeout-authority parser does not recognise this project's handoff heading

L1.recipe: Hand-add a '# Session 104 Closeout' heading to the handoff.

L2.recipe: Teach parseHandoffCloseoutAuthority the 'Latest Handoff — Session N → Session M' form (N is the closed session; M is only intent and never counts), and route brief-semantic-fingerprint through the same parser so the heading is declared once.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a test that parses the LIVE context/LATEST_HANDOFF.md and asserts it names the same session as the newest SIL entry — so a future heading change or a skipped handoff write goes red instead of silently degrading the authority to two sources.

items.executionEvidence: parseHandoffCloseoutAuthority recognises the Latest Handoff — Session N → Session M form (N only); brief-semantic-fingerprint routes through the same parser instead of its own never-matching literal. session-authority.test.js binds the LIVE handoff to the newest SIL entry and the fingerprint, with a negative control reproducing the pre-S105 pattern. Brief now renders handoff=S104.

items.title: The SIL rolling-status header has no writer and has said 'Last session: 100' for four sessions
items.premise: render-startup-brief reads 'Intent rate:', 'Last session:', 'Velocity trend:' and the averages from the rolling-status block at the top of SELF_IMPROVEMENT_LOOP.md. Nothing in this repo writes that block; it is hand-maintained and was last touched at S100. It has never carried an 'Intent rate:' line, so the brief's MOMENTUM METER renders 'Intent: ?% achieved last 5' while every one of the last five entries records 'Intent outcome: Achieved'. The same detector-without-a-writer shape S104 found in lastSessionSummary.

premises.claim: The rolling-status header still names S100 as the last session

L2.recipe: Write scripts/render-sil-rolling-status.mjs that derives the whole block from the entries themselves — last session, total, delta, 3/5/10/25/all averages, sparkline and intent rate — so the header is a projection, never an authority.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a studio-shard test asserting the committed header equals a fresh render of the committed entries, so a closeout that appends an entry and forgets the header goes red.

items.executionEvidence: scripts/render-sil-rolling-status.mjs derives the block from live+archive entries (58 unique /1000 sessions, calibration excluded), adds Intent rate (denominator = entries recording an outcome) and carries only Velocity/Debt, labelled carried. The derived Avg3 is 959.7 against the hand-written 974.7, and the hand-written 87-session population was not reproducible from /1000 scores. A studio test binds the committed block to a fresh render.

items.title: Open premise decay across the audit history can never fail anything
items.premise: check-audit-premises.mjs checks only the newest sidecar by default and is advisory; its only caller (brief-preflight) cannot be imported in this repo by contract. session104-audit-premise-decay proves the checker can fire on a fixture, but nothing asserts the real corpus stays free of open contradictions — S104's 'zero across all 83 sidecars' was a one-off manual reading.

premises.claim: No test walks every committed audit sidecar through the premise checker

L1.recipe: Run the checker across all sidecars by hand at closeout.

L2.recipe: Studio-shard test: checkAudit over every docs/AUDIT_*.json, assert openContradicted == 0 and unverified == 0.

L3.recipe: L2 with a negative control that feeds a sidecar whose premise is contradicted and whose item is still open, and asserts the corpus assertion fails on it.

items.executionEvidence: session105-brief-authority-writers walks every docs/AUDIT_*.json through checkAudit and fails on open decay or unverified premises, with a fixture negative control. On its first run it caught a live instance: this session's own sidecar, whose items 1-3 had shipped while still marked planned.

items.title: Elite density's standing watch has not been re-derived under the roster shape S104 shipped
items.premise: S103 named active-roster position composition as the measured candidate driver of elite density; S104 removed that driver (quarterback and specialist rooms bounded by FIELDABLE_DEPTH, draft intake proportional to demand) but did not re-measure elite density afterwards. The watch is currently carried on a pre-S104 reading.

premises.claim: The task board still carries elite density as an unmeasured deferral

L1.recipe: Run runRealismVerification({seasons:10}) on the canonical seed and record the elite arm.

L2.recipe: L1 on two further seeds, decompose the elite cohort by position room, and state whether the residual is intake/filter or roster shape.

L3.recipe: L2 and, only if a mechanism is measured, ship a cost with a matched control — never a threshold change.

items.executionEvidence: Shipped at the L1 rung plus the L2 room decomposition on the canonical seed; the L2 cross-seed readings were NOT taken and are the stated next step. Canonical seed 20260306, ten seasons: active-roster 90+ share 0.4% -> 2.8%, watch (S103 carried 3.3% on the pre-S104 shape). A probe reproducing the clone path (2.79% vs gated 2.8%) puts 64% of the elite cohort in QB (11/95, 11.6%) and OL (19/311, 6.1%), which are 24% of the roster; those are the only rooms generated above their own mean potential (OL 82.1 vs 79.8, QB 82.7 vs 80.9). No statistic or generator change shipped on one seed.

items.title: The brief's PROJECT PROFILE row can only ever say 'refresh required'
items.premise: render-startup-brief reads .cache/project-profile.json, a 30-minute TTL cache written only by studio-ops' scripts/lib/project-profile.mjs, which this repo does not carry. The brief is rendered at closeout, so the row is structurally stale and instructs a refresh nothing here can perform. The fix belongs in studio-ops (the renderer and the lens are both propagated), so it ships as Ark cargo, never a sibling-tree edit.

premises.claim: This repo carries no profile-lens writer

L1.recipe: Ship Ark cargo to studio-ops describing the reader-without-writer.

L2.recipe: L1 with the proposed fix: the renderer computes the lens (or renders 'no profile source' honestly) instead of reading a TTL cache it cannot refresh.

L3.recipe: Same as L2; no local change is legal here.

items.executionEvidence: Shipped as Ark pattern-share cargo 01K291HHVU080E58C015E99770 to vaultspark-studio-ops with the proposed fix (compute the lens in the renderer, or render an honest no-profile-source line). No local change is legal: renderer and lens are both propagated. Recorded in DECISIONS S105-5.

items.title: Close the open question of whether the brief renderer should call brief-preflight
items.premise: The S104 handoff asks, for the third time, whether render-startup-brief should import scripts/lib/brief-preflight.mjs. It cannot: brief-preflight statically imports scripts/check-last-session-summary.mjs, which PROJECT_AUTHORITY_CONTRACT.json forbids, and S104's import gate fails the suite the moment anything imports it. The question has a determined answer and should be recorded as a decision rather than carried.

premises.claim: The brief renderer does not import brief-preflight

L2.recipe: L1 and drop the item from the handoff's next-work list.

items.executionEvidence: Closed as DECISIONS S105-4: the renderer cannot import brief-preflight because it statically imports a contractually forbidden file, and the S104 import gate fails the suite the moment it is wired. The module stays in the tree, inert by design.
